$comment: The guided tours (tour.js): 'user' for participants, 'admin' for administrators. A step is centred, or points at 'target' (a CSS selector) on 'page' (#/<page>); it is skipped if that element is not on screen, as for a role without the feature. 'click': selectors to click first, in order. 'open': 'dock' opens the assistant. Filters: 'demo' (only on a demo server, or only elsewhere), 'cycle' (meal cycles on or off), 'feature' (roles with that feature), 'needs_people' (only if Monitor has someone to show).

user.title: Welcome to FoodRec
user.text: FoodRec suggests recipes ranked by what matters to you, and shows exactly why. This tour goes through each part of the app, one step at a time. Use Next to follow it, or Skip to explore on your own.

user.title: Your meal plan
user.text: You go through breakfast, lunch and dinner, day by day. The steps show which meal you are on, and the bar shows how many reactions you have given so far.

user.title: Pick a meal
user.text: Choose a meal to see recipes for it. Your top dishes are ranked again each time.

user.title: A recommended dish
user.text: Each card is one dish, with its picture, the main facts, and in plain words why it was suggested.

user.title: Health grade
user.text: A to E, where A is the healthiest. FoodRec works it out from the dish's nutrition. It is similar to a Nutri-Score, but it is not the official one.

user.title: React to the dish
user.text: Like it, Save it for later, say I'll cook this, or Not for me, with a reason. The app learns your taste from these. Your saved goal only changes if you agree.

user.title: Move on to the next meal
user.text: Once you have reacted to every dish in this meal, Continue takes you to the next one. After the last meal of the last day, you are done.

user.title: Why this rank?
user.text: Open How it's scored to see every factor behind the scores, how much each of your values contributed, and what is estimated or missing.

user.title: The assistant
user.text: Ask in plain words: "something easy with lentils", "why is #2 first?", "compare #1 and #3". Every step it takes is shown above its answer.

user.title: The supervisor
user.text: When your choices drift away from your saved goal, the supervisor asks a question or proposes a change here, with the evidence. Nothing changes until you accept.

user.title: Your profile
user.text: Profile holds everything the app knows about you, in tabs. Preferences has your safety rules, health goal, tastes and ingredient limit. Rules such as allergies are never relaxed automatically.

user.title: Your values
user.text: Set how much healthiness, sustainability and convenience count, and how varied your lists are. Preview the effect first. Save as new goal keeps them as a new version.

user.title: Knowledge
user.text: Search the knowledge the assistant uses, and add your own documents for it to read.

user.title: History
user.text: Every earlier version of your profile and goal is kept here, and you can go back to one.

user.title: Insights
user.text: Compare the values you chose with how your choices actually weigh them, and see the evidence behind every change. You can correct what was learned.

user.title: Activity
user.text: Everything you did and every supervisor decision, newest first.

user.title: Your account
user.text: This menu has My dishes (saved, liked and cooked), this tour, and the full guide to how FoodRec works.

user.title: See the other side
user.text: In the demo, this menu also switches to the administrator's view, where you can see how a study is run.

user.title: You are ready
user.text: Try a few reactions on Discover and ask the assistant something. You can restart this tour any time from the account menu.

admin.title: Welcome, administrator
admin.text: This side of FoodRec is for running a study. It has two pages: Monitor to follow what people do, and Config to set everything up. There are no recipes or preferences here, because those belong to participants.

admin.title: Two pages
admin.text: Monitor and Config are always up here. Unsaved changes in Config are kept while you look at Monitor.

admin.title: Sample data
admin.text: A public demo has no real study, so these populations are made up, to show what monitoring looks like. In your own copy you see your real participants.

admin.title: The whole study at a glance
admin.text: How many populations and people there are, how many have started and finished, and how many reactions they have given.

admin.title: Compare populations
admin.text: One row per population, side by side: progress, reactions per person, the share of rejected dishes, assistant use and open supervisor questions. Click a row to jump to that group.

admin.title: One population
admin.text: Each group lists its people, with role, status and meal-cycle progress. Status runs from Invited to Started, In progress and Finished, or Deactivated if you ended their access.

admin.title: Open a person
admin.text: Click anyone to read what they did. Next opens the first person for you.

admin.title: One person's record
admin.text: Their status, population and role, with the key numbers underneath.

admin.title: Interactions
admin.text: Every reaction: the dish, where it was in the list, and the reason the person gave.

admin.title: Log
admin.text: The full timeline: each list shown, action taken, message and supervisor decision. Use Show to narrow it down.

admin.title: Conversation
admin.text: What the person asked the assistant, and what it answered.

admin.title: Supervisor
admin.text: What the supervisor asked or proposed to this person, why, and how they responded.

admin.title: Values
admin.text: The weights the person saved, next to the weights their choices actually show. The gap is what the supervisor watches.

admin.title: Config
admin.text: Everything is set here, in six tabs. Each section has a Guide button that explains its settings. Saving writes the config file, and the app restarts by itself when a setting needs it.

admin.title: Read-only in the demo
admin.text: You can look at every setting and try things in the page, but the demo's file does not change. To configure FoodRec, clone the project and run it on your computer.

admin.title: Try these yourself
admin.text: These settings really do work in the demo, for your visit and your links only: the size of a meal cycle, how soon the supervisor speaks, and more. Switch to the user view to see the effect.

admin.title: Settings
admin.text: The language model, dataset, services, ranking, meal cycles and the supervisor's thresholds.

admin.title: Criteria and interactions
admin.text: What dishes are scored on, and how strongly each reaction teaches the model.

admin.title: Access roles
admin.text: A role decides what a person can see: for example, full transparency or a plain baseline list. These are the conditions of your experiment.

admin.title: Create a population
admin.text: Give the group a name, a size and the percentage per role, and choose how people get in: a password or a personal link.

admin.title: Create links
admin.text: Set a size and the percentage per role, and get a personal link per person. This does work in the demo. Open a link in a private window, and that person's real activity appears in Monitor under Your links. In your normal browser it works too: leave it from the account menu to come back here.

admin.title: Accounts and links
admin.text: Copy links, download them as a sheet, or deactivate someone. Deactivating ends that person's access straight away.

admin.title: Export
admin.text: Download the study data as JSON, or as a ZIP of CSV tables for analysis.

admin.title: JSON file
admin.text: The same settings as one file, if you prefer to edit it directly.

admin.title: Your account
admin.text: This menu restarts the tour and opens the full guide. In the demo it switches to the user view, and in your own copy it signs you out.

admin.title: You are ready
admin.text: To see a participant's side in your own copy, create a personal link and open it in a private window. Restart this tour any time from the account menu.
